title: Data in transit could be intercepted and used to identify students
description: Assignment submission data (work file, student id, course, timestamp) transmitted over network could be intercepted by attackers, enabling identification of students and their submissions.

title: Data in transit could be intercepted and disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: Assignment data transmitted over network without adequate encryption could be intercepted and disclosed to unauthorized third parties.

title: Grades Portal may store more data than necessary for assignment processing
description: The Grades Portal Web App may retain assignment submissions, student IDs, and metadata longer than necessary, potentially violating data minimization principles.

title: System may link assignment data across records to identify students
description: The Grades Portal may link assignment submissions with other student records (grades, personal info) enabling identification and profiling of students.

title: Student identity could be usurped during login
description: Student credentials used to log in could be compromised, allowing unauthorized individuals to submit assignments on behalf of legitimate students.

title: Identifier exposure in data flow
description: The data flow contains student id, course, and file reference which are unique identifiers that can be used to identify the student. These identifiers are transmitted in transit between the portal and grading service.
assumptions: Student identifiers are transmitted without additional encryption or masking in the data flow.
uncertainty_note: Citation I.2.1.1 from context is appropriate for identifier threat classification.

title: Processing of identified data at destination
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) receives and processes data containing student identifiers (student id, course, file reference). This processing of identified data creates privacy risks as the system handles personally identifiable information.
assumptions: P2 processes the received data for grading purposes, which inherently involves handling identified student data.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 from context applies to processing of identified data at destination.

title: Non-repudiation of data sharing
description: The Grades Portal (P1) shares data including requesting role information. This creates non-repudiation concerns as the role attribution could be used to establish claims about who initiated the data sharing, potentially limiting the ability to deny involvement in the data exchange.
assumptions: The requesting role is recorded and could be used to attribute the data sharing action to a specific role or individual.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation threat classification based on context §4; specific tree node Nr.1.1 inferred for role-based attribution.

title: Unnecessary Data Storage in Assignment Store
description: The Assignment Store (DS1) stores personal data (student id, course, submission time) that may be retained longer than necessary for the grading process, creating potential for future unauthorized access or disclosure beyond the immediate grading purpose.
assumptions: Data retention policies may not be strictly enforced; the stored data could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems in the future.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard data retention practices may not be in place

title: Linkability via Submission Metadata
description: The data flow contains metadata (student id, course, submission time) that could be used to link the student to their course enrollment and submission patterns, potentially enabling profiling or correlation with other data sources.
assumptions: Metadata about the student's course and submission time could be correlated with other systems or data sources.
uncertainty_note: Assuming metadata could be extracted and correlated

title: Student Identification via Stored Data
description: The student id included in the assignment file could be used to directly identify the student, potentially exposing their identity to unauthorized parties if the data store is compromised.
assumptions: Student id is a direct identifier that could be exposed through unauthorized access to the Assignment Store.
uncertainty_note: Assuming student id is a direct identifier

title: Excessive Data Collection at Source
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) collects and shares more personal data (student id, course, submission time) than strictly necessary for the grading function, potentially violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: The data collected may exceed what is necessary for the core grading function.
uncertainty_note: Assuming the data collection scope may be broader than necessary

title: Processing of identified teacher-submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified data by linking teacher identity (from login) with submission queue data, creating a profile of which teacher reviews which submissions.

title: Linkability of teacher identity with submission data
description: Metadata in the data flow (e.g., teacher ID, submission IDs, timestamps) could be used to link the teacher's identity with specific submissions they are reviewing, potentially revealing patterns about their grading behavior or course assignments.

title: Teacher identification through login credentials
description: When the teacher logs in to request the submission queue, their identity is shared with the system, enabling identification of the teacher as the data subject.

title: Linkability of student identities through submission data in transit
description: Student names and work content transmitted in the data flow could be linked to identify individual students, potentially enabling unauthorized correlation of student identities with their submissions.

title: Identification of students through direct name sharing
description: The Grades Portal Web App shares student names with the teacher, directly identifying students and enabling the teacher to link submissions to specific individuals.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student data by teacher
description: The teacher (external entity) could share or disclose student submission data (names, work content, submission times) with unauthorized parties beyond the intended scope.

title: Falsification of submission timestamps
description: Submission times displayed by the portal could be manipulated or falsified by the system, potentially misleading the teacher about when work was actually submitted.

title: Teacher Identity Exposure via Grader ID
description: When a teacher records a grade, their grader ID is included in the data, potentially revealing their identity to unauthorized parties who can access the system.

title: Linkability of Teacher-Student Relationship
description: The data flow contains student ID and grader ID together, enabling linkage between specific students and their teachers, which could be exploited to track grading patterns or relationships.

title: Student Identification in Transit
description: Student ID transmitted in the data flow could be used to identify students, especially if intercepted or logged by unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: The Grades Portal Web App stores sensitive grade and feedback data, which could be accessed by unauthorized users if proper access controls are not implemented.

title: Data Integrity Compromise at Destination
description: The system could store or display incorrect grades or feedback, potentially misleading students, parents, or educational authorities about academic performance.

title: Grade data interception in transit
description: Grade records containing student IDs, grades, and feedback could be intercepted during transmission between the grading service and database, potentially exposing sensitive academic information to unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized access to grade records
description: The Grade Records Database may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, exposing student grades, feedback, and grader information to those without proper authorization.

title: Student identification through grade records
description: The grading service shares data containing student IDs, which directly identifies students and could be used to link their academic performance to their identity.

title: Linkability of student records
description: Metadata about the data flow or the data itself (student IDs, timestamps) could be used to link multiple records to the same student, potentially revealing patterns in their academic performance.

title: Unauthorized use of grade data
description: Stored grade records could be accessed and used for purposes beyond their intended academic function, such as profiling, discrimination, or unauthorized sharing.

title: Student identity required to access grades
description: The student must identify themselves to request their own grades, which inherently links their identity to the data being requested. This is a valid interaction where the source element's act of sharing causes the threat.

title: Request metadata could be linked
description: Metadata about the request (timestamp, IP address, device information) could be used to link this request to other activities or identify the student through correlation.

title: Grades could be disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The Grades Portal Web App receives and processes the grades data, potentially storing or transmitting it in a way that allows unauthorized access or disclosure to third parties.

title: Grade data interception during transmission
description: Student grades and teacher feedback transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive academic information.

title: Metadata linking student to grades
description: Metadata accompanying the data flow (e.g., timestamps, session IDs) could be used to link the student to their grades, potentially enabling tracking of academic performance patterns.

title: Portal exposes grades to unauthorized users
description: The Grades Portal Web App may inadvertently expose student grades to unauthorized users through improper access controls or logging mechanisms.

title: Student shares grades with unauthorized parties
description: The student receiving the grades may share this sensitive information with unauthorized third parties, violating privacy expectations.

title: Parent-child account linkage enables inference of child's academic information
description: The parent's account is linked to the child's account, allowing the system to associate the parent's identity with the child's grades. This linkage could be exploited to infer sensitive information about the child's academic performance.

title: Request metadata reveals parent identity and accessed data
description: Metadata about the request (e.g., timestamp, parent ID, child ID) could be used to identify the parent and what grades they're accessing, potentially revealing patterns in parental monitoring.

title: Grades may be disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: If the system doesn't properly restrict access, grades could be disclosed to unauthorized parties, violating the child's privacy.

title: Parent credentials could be compromised
description: Parent login credentials could be intercepted or stolen, allowing unauthorized access to child's grades.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's academic data
description: The Grades Portal Web App may disclose sensitive academic information (grades, feedback, submission history) to the parent without proper authorization controls or verification that the parent is the legitimate guardian.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Academic data transmitted from the portal to the parent could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially exposing sensitive student information.

title: Parent misuse of child's academic data
description: The parent receiving the data may use it for purposes beyond their intended role, such as sharing with third parties or using it for unauthorized purposes.

title: Excessive data sharing beyond necessity
description: The portal may share more detailed academic information than necessary for the parent's legitimate oversight role, violating data minimization principles.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Personal data (names, emails, roles, relationships) transmitted between administrator and web app could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, enabling identification of parents and children.

title: Linkability of Parent-Child Data
description: Metadata and data in transit could be used to link parent-child relationships with other data sources, potentially revealing family connections and enabling profiling.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure at Destination
description: The Grades Portal Web App may store sensitive parent-child relationship data without adequate access controls, risking disclosure to unauthorized personnel or systems.

title: Data Misuse for Unauthorized Purposes
description: The process may use collected parent-child relationship data for purposes beyond the intended administrative function, such as marketing or third-party sharing.

title: False or Misleading Data Entry
description: Administrator may intentionally or unintentionally enter incorrect parent-child relationship data, creating false records that could mislead system users and affect decision-making.

title: Identifiability of account records in transit
description: Account records and parent-child relationship links transmitted from the grading service to the account directory may contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify individuals if intercepted or exposed during transit.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of account data at destination
description: The account directory may store account records and parent-child relationship links in a manner that allows unauthorized access or disclosure to entities without proper authorization.

title: Linkability of account records at destination
description: The account directory may store account records and parent-child relationship links in a way that enables linking of data across different records to identify individuals or infer relationships.

title: Usurpation of data sharing purpose at source
description: The grading service may share account records and parent-child relationship links with the account directory for purposes beyond the intended grading and assignment management, potentially enabling misuse of the data.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are intentionally transferred to the cloud hosting provider as part of nightly backup and replication. This constitutes explicit data disclosure to a third party, raising concerns about data minimality and whether all transferred data is strictly necessary for the hosting service.

title: Linkability via Metadata in Data Transfer
description: During the nightly backup transfer, metadata about the data (e.g., timestamps, data volumes, access patterns) could be used to link or identify individuals. The account directory being transferred enables potential cross-referencing of student identities across systems.

title: Identification Risk at Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider receives account directory and grade records that contain personally identifiable information. There is a risk that the provider could identify individuals through this data, potentially for purposes beyond the intended hosting service.

title: Unnecessary Data Sharing at Source
description: The Assignment & Grading Service shares comprehensive data (full grade records, assignments, account directory) with the cloud provider. This may violate the minimality principle if not all this data is strictly required for the backup/hosting purpose, creating avoidable disclosure risk.
